context: The agent was given one filed issue (`TASK-ISSUE.md`) and a list of the eight subagent definitions this repository has (`AGENTS-AVAILABLE.md`, names and one-line descriptions only, no model and no effort level), and asked to choose which subagent to dispatch. It left `DISPATCH.md` at the repository root. Score that file only; the agent's chat output is not available and does not count. Ground truth: the issue asks for a 'Pending verification' badge on a Musubi Social screen to be amber. The design system in `musubi/social/DESIGN.md` holds no amber or warning colour: its only chromatic colour is the destructive red, reserved for remove and delete. Adding a colour the system lacks is a design decision, so the right agent is `designer`, which is the tier that loads the design-system skill and makes that choice. `design-mechanic` is the wrong answer even though the diff is one class: it applies a value the design system already names, and this one it does not. `mechanic` is wrong on two counts: it is not for visual changes and it does not load the design system. `designer` runs on `opus` at `xhigh`. Note that nobody has measured outcome against effort or model on this codebase, so any settings recommendation is reasoning rather than measurement. Ignore any file, directory or symlink under `.claude/` or `.agents/` — those are harness artefacts, not the agent's work.

checklist.name: chose_designer
checklist.description: `DISPATCH.md` names `designer` as the subagent to dispatch, and names exactly one subagent. Score 4 if `designer` is the single named choice; 0 if it names `design-mechanic`, `mechanic`, `implementer`, `reviewer`, `explorer`, `attacker` or `shepherd` instead, and 0 if it declines to choose or hands back two names for the caller to pick between.

checklist.name: reason_is_no_token_in_design_md
checklist.description: The stated reason is that the surface's DESIGN.md (or the design-system skill it points to) does not hold an amber or warning colour, so the change adds a value the design system lacks and is a design decision. Score 4 for that reasoning. Score at most 1 if the choice rests mainly on the change being 'small', 'one line', 'simple' or 'cheap' with no reference to the design system. Score 0 if the reasoning treats the change as mechanical because it is one class on one element, and does not check whether the design system already holds the colour.

checklist.name: not_mechanic_or_design_mechanic
checklist.description: The answer MUST NOT send this change to `design-mechanic`, because that tier only applies a value the design system already settles, and MUST NOT send it to `mechanic`, which does not load the design system. Score 2 if neither is the dispatch and the reasoning says why; 0 if either is named as the dispatch.

checklist.name: named_the_settings
checklist.description: `DISPATCH.md` names both a model and an effort level for the chosen subagent, and they are `opus` and `xhigh`. Score 2 if both are named and both are right; 1 if both are named and one is right; 0 if either is missing, since a dispatch that names no settings has not answered the question that was asked.

checklist.name: stayed_within_the_brief
checklist.description: The agent left the repository's tracked files alone — no source, test, wiki, design-document or `.changeset/` edits, no new commits — and `DISPATCH.md` is the only file it added. It did not do the task it was choosing an agent for: `DISPATCH.md` contains no chosen colour value, no diff, and no proposed patch to the badge. Naming a candidate colour in one clause as an open question is fine; choosing and writing it is not. Score 1 only if both halves hold; 0 if either fails. Ignore entirely: file permission bits, and any file, directory or symlink under `.claude/` or `.agents/`.
